clues.text: The ball must be inflated to between 0.6 and 1.1 atmospheres at sea level, with a circumference of 68–70 cm.
Only one player on each team is allowed to wear tracksuit bottoms.
A match can't start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players.
A goal can't be scored directly when the ball is thrown back into play with both hands from the sideline.
If the one player allowed to handle the ball holds it for more than eight seconds, the opponents get a corner kick.
You're penalised if, when a teammate plays the ball to you, you're nearer the opponents' goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent.
A player who reaches the foul limit but has no eligible substitute stays in the game, and their team is charged a technical foul.
With only 0.1 or 0.2 seconds left on the clock, the only way to score is a deflection or a high lob; there isn't time to catch and shoot.
clues.ref: NBA Comments on the Rules, L (Expiration of time)

clues.text: Each side has five players on the court, and a professional game is four 12-minute quarters.
An attacking player may not stay inside the painted lane near the target for more than three seconds.
Once you stop dribbling, you can't start dribbling again.
A shot from beyond the curved line about 7 metres from the basket is worth three points.
Your [hitting implement] may be no longer than 73.7 cm (29 in), and its strings must be strung in a generally uniform pattern.
If a spare ball falls out of your own pocket mid-point, you can't claim it as a hindrance and ask for a replay.
At 6–6 in a set, a tie-break is usually played: first to 7 points, winning by 2.
When starting a point, you must stand behind the back line and may not walk or run; touching the line with your foot is a fault.
A serve that clips the net and then lands in the correct service box is a let and is replayed.
Points are counted 15, 30, 40, then game, and at 40–40 you must win two points in a row.
You get three minutes to search for your ball. If it isn't found in that time, it's lost.
When making a stroke, you may not brace your [implement] against your body, for example by pressing the handle into your chest.
You may carry no more than 14 [implements] during a round.
If your ball lies in a sand-filled hollow, you may not touch the sand with your [implement] on the backswing.
On the putting green you may mark, lift and clean your ball, and repair old hole plugs and spike marks.
Play a ball from the tee into the hole in as few strokes as possible. A standard round is 18 holes.
A player whose [stick] breaks may keep playing only if they drop the broken pieces right away. Otherwise it's a two-minute penalty.
A game is three 20-minute periods of actual playing time.
If a team sends the [object] from its own half all the way past the opponents' goal line untouched, play stops and restarts in the offending team's end.
A puck that goes into the net off a distinct kicking motion is no goal.
A team that takes a penalty plays short-handed on the ice for two minutes.
Six a side on the ice, including a goaltender, chasing a vulcanised rubber puck with sticks.
If a fielder deliberately throws their glove at a fair hit ball and touches it, every runner, including the hitter, is awarded three bases.
The glove of the player who delivers the ball to the hitter may not be white or gray.
Nine players per side, and a regulation game gives each side nine turns to attack.
The hitter is out if they hit the ball with a foot entirely outside the marked box they're standing in.
With runners on first and second and fewer than two out, a fair pop-up an infielder can catch with ordinary effort is an automatic out, even if it's dropped.
Three strikes and the batter is out. Four balls and they walk to first base.
A new [hitter] who isn't ready to play within 3 minutes of the previous one being dismissed is themselves out.
A new ball must weigh between 5.5 and 5.75 ounces (155.9–163 g).
The fielding side may leave a spare helmet on the ground only directly behind their keeper. If the ball hits it, the other side gets 5 penalty runs.
The delivery is illegal if the player sending it straightens their elbow after their arm passes shoulder height.
A [hitter] can be given out if the ball strikes their leg when it would otherwise have gone on to hit the stumps.
Six legal deliveries make an over, and an innings ends when ten of the eleven batters are out.
In a 10-period game, each team gets 38 minutes of 'thinking time'. The clock runs only while they're deciding.
Each [object] may weigh no more than 19.96 kg (44 lb), including its handle and bolt.
Four players a side, and each player delivers two [objects] per period. Only one team can score in a period.
Before the sixth delivery of a period, you may not knock an opponent's [object] out of play from the protected zone in front of the target.
A stone must be clearly released from the hand before it reaches the hog line at the delivery end.
Teammates sweep the ice ahead of a moving stone. Only the team with the stone closest to the button scores.
The ball's internal pressure must be 0.30–0.325 kg/cm² (4.26–4.61 psi).
The barrier dividing the two sides stands 2.43 m high for men and 2.24 m for women.
Periods are won at 25 points with a two-point lead, and a deciding fifth goes to 15.
A team may touch the ball at most three times before sending it back, and touching the ball at the barrier to stop it doesn't count.
The libero, in a contrasting shirt, may not complete an attack hit when the ball is entirely above the top of the net.
When a team wins back the right to serve, its six players rotate one position clockwise.
At least 85% of the blade's thickness must be natural wood.
If a game isn't finished after 10 minutes, unless both sides have 9+ points, the 'expedite system' starts and each serve change brings new limits.
A game is won at 11 points with a two-point lead, and service changes hands every two points.
To serve, you must project the ball almost straight up from a flat, open palm so it rises at least 16 cm.
Your racket's two rubbers must be different colours, one black and the other a bright colour.
Played with a 40 mm ball on a table 2.74 m long, over a net 15.25 cm high.
After a fair catch, the receiving team may choose to try a free kick at the posts from that spot, and the defenders can't rush it.
Deliberately fumbling the ball forward is treated as a forward pass.
Eleven players a side, and a game is four 15-minute periods.
Only one forward throw is allowed per play, and it must come from behind the spot where the play started.
If a ball carrier is downed in their own end zone, the defense scores 2 points.
The offense gets four downs to gain 10 yards, and a touchdown is worth 6 points.
It's a foul to make the white ball leap over any part of another ball.
It's a foul if your tip is still touching the white when it strikes another ball.
A game starts with 22 balls on the table: 15 identical ones, six others each worth a different amount, and the one you strike.
If it's unclear which ball you're aiming for, you must declare it to the referee before playing.
After a foul, if you can't hit both sides of the ball you need, you may nominate any other ball to act as it.
After a foul, the referee can call a miss and make the offender replay the shot if they didn't make a good enough attempt to hit the ball they needed.
Pot a red, then a colour, and repeat. There are 15 reds, and the black is worth 7.
When restarting quickly from the sideline, you must use the same ball that went out. Swap in another ball and the throw is wrong.
After a score, the kicker has 60 seconds of playing time to take the follow-up kick at goal.
A match lasts no more than 80 minutes: two halves of up to 40 minutes each, plus time lost.
The ball may never be thrown or passed forward. It can only go sideways or backwards.
If a maul stops moving toward the line for more than five seconds, the referee tells the team to use the ball.
Grounding the ball in the opponents' in-goal is a try worth 5 points, and the conversion after it is worth 2.
The ball must weigh between 156 and 163 grams.
A player's [playing implement] must not weigh more than 737 grams.
Eleven players a side, and a match is four 15-minute quarters.
A goal only counts if an attacker played the ball from inside the marked area in front of goal.
At a penalty corner, no more than five defenders, including the goalkeeper, may start behind the backline.
Players must not play the ball with the rounded back of the stick, only its flat side.
To test its speed, the [object] is hit underarm from the back line. If it's correct, it lands 530–990 mm short of the far back line.
A game is won at 21 points, and at 29-all the next point wins.
At the moment it's struck on a serve, the whole [object] must be below 1.15 m from the floor.
It's a fault if the shuttle passes over the net and then gets caught in it.
Played with rackets and a shuttlecock of 16 feathers fixed into a cork base.
Each player brings their own [objects], each no longer than 30.5 cm and no heavier than 50 grams.
The target's centre is 1.73 m off the floor, and you throw from 2.37 m away.
Each turn is three throws, and only throws that land inside the outermost scoring ring count.
To win a leg, your final dart must land in the double of the exact number you need.
Each player starts on 501 and counts down to zero, finishing on a double or the bull.
If you're found with a phone or other electronic device on you in the playing venue, you lose the game.
You must stop your [timer] with the same hand you used to make your move.
If 75 consecutive moves by each side pass with no capture and no move of the smallest [unit], the game is automatically drawn.
If you deliberately touch one of your own pieces, you must move it, as long as it has a legal move.
You may not castle if your king would pass through a square the opponent attacks.
You win by checkmating your opponent's king.
Each competitor must be weighed by the Technical Delegate at the end of their last qualifying session.
A competitor whose best qualifying time is more than 107% of the fastest needs special permission to start the main event.
A speed limit of 80 km/h applies in the service lane for the whole event.
In a dry race, every driver must use at least two different specifications of dry-weather tyres.
When the safety car is out, race control may tell lapped cars to overtake it and rejoin the back of the pack.
You must hold your weapon in one hand and may not switch hands during the bout, except with the referee's permission after an injury.
Competitors face off on a strip 14 metres long and 1.5–2 metres wide.
Deliberately bumping into your opponent is penalised with two of the three weapon types, but not the third.
With foil and sabre, if both competitors hit at once, 'right of way' decides who scores.
clues.ref: t.82 (Validity or priority of the hit)

clues.text: With the épée, the whole body is target and both fencers can score a touch at the same moment.
The player starting play from the centre must release the ball within three seconds.
Seven players a side, four 15-minute quarters and a 12-minute half-time.
A defender must stay at least 0.9 m (3 ft) from the player holding the ball.
You can't dribble or run with the ball. Once you land, you may pivot, but you can't re-ground your landing foot before passing.
Only the Goal Shooter and Goal Attack may score, and only from inside the goal circle.
Athletes may wear tape on one or two fingers or toes only, and only to treat or protect an injury.
Anyone who starts before the signal is disqualified. There's no second chance.
After the start, and each time you push off a wall, you may stay fully underwater for no more than 15 metres.
In breaststroke, after the start and each turn, you're allowed one arm stroke and a single butterfly kick underwater.
In an individual medley, the order is butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, then freestyle.
Reacting to the gun in less than 0.100 seconds counts as a false start.
If the tailwind averages more than 2 metres per second, a performance can't be ratified as a record.
In one event, an athlete must take off from one foot. A two-footed take-off isn't allowed.
In the 4×100 m relay, the baton must change hands inside a 30 m takeover zone.
The sport's events are running, jumping and throwing, and sprinters must stay in their own lane.
If daylight shows between the top of the ball and the bottom edge of the [stick] head's sidewall, the [stick] is illegal.
Ten players make a full team.
Once a team gains possession, it has 80 seconds to take a shot.
Attacking players may not enter the circular crease around the goal.
Players catch, carry and throw the ball with a netted crosse, and play restarts with a face-off.
Every [projectile] must be marked with the athlete's name or initials.
[Projectile] shafts may be no more than 9.3 mm in diameter, and their tips no more than 9.4 mm.
In head-to-head matches, whoever scores more in a set earns 2 set points and a tie earns 1 each. The first to 6 set points wins.
If a shot touches the line between two scoring zones, it scores the higher value.
Recurve athletes aim at a target face 122 cm across.
Athletes shoot arrows from a bow at a ringed target, scoring 10 for the gold centre.
The official at the scoring end signals a major score by raising both index fingers, then waving two flags.
Eighteen players a side may be on the field at once, plus up to four interchange players.
Cleanly catching a kick earns you a free kick, but only if the ball travelled at least 15 metres.
You can't throw the ball. To pass by hand, hold it in one hand and punch it with the clenched fist of the other.
A kick between the two tall middle posts is worth 6 points, and one between a middle and an outer post is a behind worth 1.
If you kick from inside your own 40 m and the ball bounces out inside the opponents' 20 m, your team gets the restart.
No more than 13 players per side may be on the field.
A drop kick through the posts during open play is worth just one point.
A team gets six tackles to score. After the sixth, possession passes to the opponents.
A try is worth 4 points, and after every tackle the tackled player rolls the ball back with their foot.
The senior men's ball must be 58–60 cm around and weigh 425–475 g.
You may hold the ball for at most 3 seconds and take at most 3 steps with it.
Outfield players may not touch the ball with the foot or the leg below the knee.
Once the referees warn for passive play, the attacking team has at most four more passes before it must shoot.
Only the goalkeeper may enter the 6-metre goal area.
The referee must order a replay if court conditions change during a rally through no fault of either player.
Games go to 11 points, and at 10-all you need a two-point lead.
When serving, at least one foot must be touching the floor inside the service box as you strike the ball.
A return that hits the tin is not good.
Two players share a four-walled court, taking turns to hit a small rubber ball against the front wall.
A ball with larger holes is customarily used outdoors, and one with smaller holes indoors.
Games are usually played to 11 points, and you must win by 2.
The serve and the return of serve must each bounce once before anyone may hit the ball in the air.
On a volley serve, the ball must be below the server's waist when the paddle makes contact.
You can't volley while standing in the 7-foot non-volley zone by the net, known as the kitchen.
The ball may weigh no more than 16 pounds, and there's no minimum weight.
A game has ten turns. In the last turn you get a third delivery if you clear everything.
If any part of your body touches the surface beyond the release line, the delivery counts but scores nothing.
A strike is worth 10 plus whatever you knock down with your next two balls.
Roll a ball down a lane to knock over ten pins.
Each player's [objects] must weigh between 650 and 800 grams.
Games are played to 13 points.
The small target must land between 6 and 10 metres from where it was thrown.
Players throw from a circle 35–50 cm across, with both feet inside it.
Players toss metal boules from a circle to land as close as possible to the jack, or cochonnet.
Players may not have grease, oil or any similar substance on their body or hands.
A team may keep the ball for no more than 28 seconds without shooting.
Goalkeepers must wear red caps.
Standing on the bottom of the pool is a foul.
Seven a side swim and throw a ball into the opponents' goal, and leaving the pool to sit on the side or steps is an exclusion foul.
Every boat's bow must be fitted with a solid ball shape.
The standard international race distance is 2,000 metres in a straight line.
The first 100 metres of the course is designated the start zone.
A coxswain must weigh at least 55 kg in racing kit and may carry up to 15 kg of deadweight to make up the difference.
Crews sit facing backwards and pull on oars to drive the boat over the finish line.
clues.ref: Part I (scope and definition of rowing)

clues.text: Competitors must have their fingernails cut very short.
A senior bout is two 3-minute periods with a 30-second break.
In one of the styles, grabbing your opponent below the belt line or using your legs to trip them is strictly forbidden.
Holding both of your opponent's shoulders against the mat ends the bout immediately.
The two Olympic styles are Greco-Roman and freestyle, contested on a circular mat.
There are no referees: players and captains alone make and resolve all calls.
The player holding the [object] may not run with it and must keep a pivot foot.
The defender guarding the thrower counts aloud from one to ten, at least a second apart. The throw must be gone before ten.
The game is self-officiated and non-contact, guided by the Spirit of the Game.
You score by catching the disc in the end zone you're attacking.
The equipment must be 10–12.5 cm in circumference, with no knots or other handholds.
Teams compete in weight classes and are weighed beforehand. A team is eight athletes plus a coach and trainer.
Everyone except the last team member must grip with both hands.
The anchor at the back may wear a protective vest up to a maximum thickness.
Two teams pull on a rope, and you win by dragging it the required distance past the markings.
The ball must have a circumference of 62–64 cm, smaller than in most football codes.
Two halves of 20 minutes of playing time, with the clock stopped whenever the ball is out of play.
Free kicks and other restarts must be taken within four seconds, or possession goes to the other side.
From a team's sixth accumulated foul in a half, opponents get a direct free kick from the 10 m mark with no defensive wall.
Five a side on a hard indoor court. When the ball goes over the sideline, play restarts with a kick-in instead of a throw-in.
Players in one code may be required to wear helmets, but the referee must not allow a helmet in a game of this one.
Senior championship games are two periods of 35 minutes each, with time added for stoppages.
A kick over the bar from on or outside a 40 m arc is worth two points, but only one point from a 45.
You may carry the ball for no longer than it takes to take four steps, then you must bounce it or solo it (toe-tap it).
Fifteen a side kick and hand-pass a round ball. Under the crossbar is a goal worth 3, and over it is a point.
Every player must wear a helmet with a face guard that meets the Irish national safety standard.
Fifteen a side over two periods, and the ball may be struck with the hand, kicked, or lifted off the ground with the feet.
Players may not touch the ball on the ground with their hands unless they've been knocked down.
You may hold the sliotar for no longer than four steps, but you can balance it on your hurley as you run.
Played with an ash stick called a hurley and a small ball called a sliotar. Over the bar is a point, and under it is a goal.
No player may swing their [implement] in a windmill or helicopter fashion.
Each period lasts at most 7½ minutes.
Play starts with the umpire bowling the ball in between the two teams, who must stay still until it leaves the umpire's hand.
No player may cross another who is riding parallel to the line of the ball.
Four a side on horseback, hitting a ball with long-handled mallets across chukkers.
The player delivering the ball has 10 seconds to release the next one.
Ten players take the field, including four outfielders.
Each delivery must travel in a visible arc, reaching between 1.83 m (6 ft) and 3.65 m (12 ft) above the ground.
Runners may not steal bases. Advancing before the batter hits the pitch is prohibited.
Like baseball but with a larger ball, a smaller field and underhand pitching.
Players must not hold, squeeze or pinch a ball in a way that could damage it.
Headbands, bandanas and protective helmets are the only headgear allowed.
A team that starts a set with fewer than six players on court is officially short-handed.
A player who has been put out may come back onto court only when a teammate cleanly grabs an opponent's throw out of the air.
Hit an opponent with a thrown ball and they're eliminated. Catch their throw and the thrower is out instead.
Teams throw foam balls at each other, trying to eliminate every opponent.
The [hitting implement] has no strings and may be no longer than 45.5 cm in total.
The playing area is fully enclosed: walls 3 m high, topped by a further metre of metal fencing.
On the serve, the ball must be at or below waist height when it's struck.
After the ball bounces on your side, you can play it off the glass walls before hitting it back.
Doubles on a small court enclosed by glass and mesh, using solid perforated rackets and an underhand serve.
The ball's inside pressure is 0.175–0.225 kg/cm², softer than its indoor cousin's.
Teams switch ends every 7 points, or every 5 in the deciding period.
Periods go to 21 points, and a deciding third goes to 15.
Unlike the indoor game, a block counts as one of the team's three touches.
Two players per team on sand. Attacking with an open-handed finger tip is a fault.
Every [object] used must bear the governing body's official stamp.
Each player has a set of four [objects] that must all match in size, colour and weight.
The small white target must come to rest at least 23 m from where it's delivered, or it's re-spotted.
A bowl that touches the jack during its original course is a toucher, and must be marked with chalk.
Roll weighted, biased balls along a flat green to finish as close as possible to the jack.
The four corners of the playing area are marked with flags coloured blue, red, black and yellow.
One side plays the blue and black balls, and the other plays red and yellow.
If your ball hits another ball, you then place yours against it and play a stroke that moves both.
Each ball must run 12 hoops in a set order (the last is called 'rover') and then hit the centre peg.
Players strike balls with a mallet through hoops on a lawn.
Each [object] is roughly 6 inches square and weighs 14–16.25 ounces.
Adults throw from a line 27 feet from the target.
Scoring is by cancellation: only the difference between the two sides' points in a round counts.
A bag that goes through the hole, even if knocked in by another bag, is worth three points.
Toss bean bags at a slanted board with a hole in it, playing to 21.
Your playing position is a rectangle 20 cm wide and 30 cm deep, directly behind your marker.
At the start of each hole, all your supporting points must be inside the starting area when you release.
Landing out-of-bounds costs one penalty throw.
Within 10 metres of the target, you must show full balance behind your marker before moving forward.
Throw a disc into a chain basket in as few throws as possible.
Whenever your opponent is given a penalty, you're awarded one point.
A contest is three rounds of two minutes, with a one-minute rest between them.
A punch scores 1 point, but only when it lands on the body protector.
A kick to the trunk protector scores 2 points, and a kick to the head scores 3.
Korean martial art in a dobok, scored by electronic sensors in body and head protectors.
The steel blades the vehicle glides on may be no more than 4 °C warmer than a reference blade. Fail the check twice and you're disqualified.
The maximum combined weight is 390 kg for a crew of two and 630 kg for a crew of four.
Results are decided by adding up the times of all the race heats.
The pilot at the front steers the sled using steering ropes and handles.
Teams of two or four push a steerable sled, jump in, and race it down an ice track.
The vehicle alone may weigh no more than 45 kg for men and 38 kg for women.
Athlete plus equipment may not exceed 120 kg for men or 102 kg for women.
Results are decided by adding up each athlete's times across the race heats.
Only the head-first, prone position, lying on your stomach, is allowed.
Slide head-first and face-down on a small sled down an ice track.
A full set of spare equipment must be placed around the floor area for anyone to use.
Each individual routine must last between 1'15" and 1'30". At 1'31.00 there's a penalty.
In group routines, a 'long throw' must cover at least 6 metres between performers.
The five apparatus are rope, hoop, ball, clubs and ribbon.
Judged routines set to music, performed while handling a ribbon, hoop, ball or clubs.
The goalkeeper may not hold the ball in their hands for more than four seconds.
A match is three periods of 12 minutes of playing time.
Unlawfully preventing an opponent from executing a scissors or overhead kick is a foul.
Footwear isn't permitted, so everyone plays barefoot.
Five a side on sand, often with spectacular bicycle kicks.
The field of play is 110 yards (100 m) long and 65 yards (60 m) wide.
Each team has 12 players on the field at any one time.
The offense gets only three attempts to advance the ball 10 yards.
If a kick ends dead in the end zone without being returned, the kicking team scores a single point, called a rouge.
Gridiron football with 12 players a side, three downs and a 110-yard field.
Players coming onto the field must take up an onside position before joining play.
Possession changes after the defending team has made its sixth legal contact on the ball carrier.
The player who picks up the ball at the restart, called the half, isn't allowed to score.
After being touched, the attacker places the ball on the ground and steps over it to restart play, a rollball.
Rugby without tackles: six touches, then the other team gets the ball.
Only the goalkeeper may take part in play without a [playing implement].
A match is two halves of 45 minutes.
You may not strike the ball with your [implement] above shoulder height.
Played on skates with sticks and a ball, on an ice field 90–110 m long, bordered by low boards.
Hockey's older cousin: eleven a side on skates, with a small ball instead of a puck, on a huge ice field.
The goalkeeper plays without any [playing implement].
Regular game time is three periods of 20 minutes.
It's a free hit if a player plays, or tries to play, the ball above knee level.
Played indoors in a rink, with a light plastic ball and lightweight sticks.
Indoor hockey with lightweight sticks and a plastic ball full of holes.
If both teams are guilty of anti-play, the referees can show a blue card to both captains.
Raising the ball above the permitted height is a technical foul, except for the goalkeeper.
Raising your [implement] above your shoulders in a way that endangers others is a technical foul.
Players use skates with four wheels in two pairs, though inline skates are also allowed.
Hockey on quad roller skates, played with a ball and a goalkeeper plus four rink players a side.
Each possession has a thirty-second shot clock.
A team may appoint no more than three captains from among its players.
The [object] can't be carried across a blue line. It must be passed, shot, or deflected across.
Skaters use a straight-bladed stick to carry, pass and shoot a rubber ring.
Canadian ice team sport played with a ring instead of a puck.
Actual playing time must be sixty minutes, with a half-time interval of no more than 15 minutes.
Players' numbers must appear on the team jersey and on the skirt or skort.
A player may not pick the ball up off the ground with her hand, or throw it up and catch it.
clues.ref: Playing rules (A player may not, a and d)

clues.text: Played with a hurley and sliotar, with points over the bar and goals under it.
The women's stick game related to hurling, governed by its own Irish association.
The head of the [implement] must be small enough to pass through a ring of a fixed size.
Each team has no more than twelve players, one of whom is the goalkeeper.
Only the goalkeeper may stop the ball with an open hand, and only within the ten-yard area.
Play starts with a throw-up between two players, and a goal scored straight from a throw-up counts.
Scotland's Highland stick game, played with a caman and closely related to hurling.
Each player's [implement] must fit entirely inside a box 100 × 350 × 50 mm.
A squad is up to six players plus four substitutes, who may be used at any time.
Advancing the [object] with your glove, free hand or body is a foul.
Played on the bottom of a pool wearing a mask, snorkel and fins, pushing a puck with a short stick.
Six-a-side hockey played on the floor of a swimming pool.
The goal judge signals a goal by waving their [implement] above their head.
A team is six players in two sections of three, and the sections play alternate periods.
Players must be within reach of an opponent's [implement] before attacking them for the ball.
Riders carry the ball in a racquet with a loose net, and sections swap between chukkas.
Polo crossed with lacrosse: played on horseback with netted racquets.
The field must be at least 70 metres long, with four running stations 25 metres apart.
A match ends when each side has had five turns at batting (seven in All-Ireland finals).
Hitters try to score a run by getting all the way round the field and home.
Batters run between four bases, 25 m apart, after the pitcher delivers the ball.
An old Irish and British bat-and-ball game, a forerunner of baseball.
The top edge of the target is 3.5 m above the ground.
Each team starts with four men and four women.
You may only hinder an opponent of your own sex. Blocking a shot from the opposite sex is a foul.
You may not shoot from a defended position, so an opponent close by with an arm up blocks the shot.
Dutch mixed team game shooting into a basket on a tall post. After every two goals, players switch zones.
A player may not shoot at the same target a fourth time in a row.
A team may make no more than three consecutive passes before shooting.
Passes may not be intercepted by the other team, which keeps the game non-aggressive.
A forbidden zone with a 3 m radius surrounds each frame, and stepping on its line with the ball is a fault.
Score by throwing the ball onto a sprung rebound frame so it bounces back and lands untouched.
Officials use a six-sided die marked with the three team colours, two faces each.
Teams wear the official colours: blue (or pink), grey and black.
A match is played by three teams of four players at the same time.
The ball is enormous, 1.22 m across.
Canadian-invented game where three teams play at once with a giant ball.
Before the game starts, the referee asks everyone to switch off mobile phones, and spectators must stay quiet while the ball is in play.
A game is 24 minutes in total: two halves of 12 minutes.
A team must throw the ball within ten seconds of first controlling it.
The 1.25 kg ball has holes so the bells inside can be heard, and every player wears eyeshades.
Paralympic sport for visually impaired athletes: three a side roll a ball with bells inside toward a goal the full width of the court.
In a recent rule update, the equipment players straddle was officially renamed from 'brooms' to 'sticks'.
A gender maximum rule limits how many players of the same gender a team can have in play at once.
A player who is knocked out must go back and touch one of their own goal rings before returning to play.
Players keep a stick between their legs at all times, and a goal through a hoop is worth ten points.
The real-world sport adapted from a fictional wizarding game. Catching the flag runner's flag earns 30 points.
Every player has a functional rating, and the ratings of the players on court can't add up to more than eight.
A team may have up to twelve members, but no more than four may be on court at once.
An attacking player may not stay in the marked area in front of the opponents' goal line for more than ten seconds.
The ball may be passed, rolled, batted, bounced or carried on the lap, as long as the holder partly supports it.
Rugby-style full-contact Paralympic sport played four a side in wheelchairs.
The first two games of a match are played to 15 points, and a tiebreaker game to 11.
A serve that passes so close to the server that it blocks the receiver's view is a fault, a screen serve.
A serve that rebounds off the main wall and then hits the overhead surface is a fault.
In rallies, the ceiling and all four walls are in play, and the serve must land beyond the short line.
Played with a short racquet and a hollow rubber ball in a fully enclosed court, ceiling included.
The team that wins the toss warms up first, for two minutes.
A match is one set, won by the first team to reach 21 points.
Once the server makes contact, all players may move freely on their own side.
The server, called the tekong, kicks the ball over the net to start each rally.
Southeast Asian net game, like volleyball played with the feet, knees and head.
You lose the point if you touch the ball twice in a row with the same body part.
A maximum of three touches is allowed before the ball must go back over.
A ball that hits the edge of the playing surface is an 'edgeball' and has its own rules.
Played over a net on a curved table, using any body part except the hands and arms.
Football skills on a curved ping-pong-style table.
Only the serving side can score points. The receiving side can only win back the serve.
A game is won by the side that first scores 21 points.
The rules cover two court sizes used in Ireland, 60 × 30 ft and 40 × 20 ft.
Players strike a small ball against the front wall using only their hand.
Irish wall game, like squash without rackets, run alongside hurling and Gaelic football.
Some athletes' assistants must keep their back to the play and may not look at the court during an end.
Athletes play from one of six numbered boxes at one end of the court.
If the assistant turns to look at play before the end is finished, the opponents are awarded a penalty ball.
Some players release the ball down a ramp, aiming for the white jack ball.
Paralympic precision ball sport, related to bocce, played from seated throwing boxes.
The goal hangs with its lower edge two metres above the surface.
A player may keep possession of the ball for no more than 5 seconds.
A player must have both shoulders above the water before an opponent may try to take the ball.
Illegally pushing an opponent's kayak is a foul, and so is illegal use of the paddle.
Five a side in kayaks, throwing a ball into goals suspended over the water.
In the visually impaired version, the athletes start the contest already gripping each other's jacket with both hands.
Blind athletes walk to the starting position next to the referee rather than being led by the hand.
Apart from the special start, the visually impaired version uses the standard international rules.
Competitors wear a judogi, and referees use special signs to award Ippon and Waza-ari.
Japanese Olympic grappling martial art in which a throw or hold-down can score Ippon.
It's a foul to stifle the attacking player by covering their mouth or throat.
Taking more than 10 seconds to start an attack is a foul.
A yellow card means a two-minute suspension, and the suspended player can't be revived in that time.
The raider crosses into the opponents' half and tries to tag defenders, then return without being caught.
clues.sourceNote: Common rule, not stated in the source file

clues.text: South Asian contact tag game where the raider must chant the game's name on a single breath.
clues.sourceNote: Common rule, not stated in the source file

clues.text: Once a turn has started, none of the seated players on the pursuing team may leave their place except as the rules allow.
A team is 12 players, and 9 take the field at the start.
An attacker must keep going in the direction they turned their shoulder, and can't reverse.
Eight chasers sit in a line of squares facing alternate ways, and the active chaser tags a seated teammate to swap in.
Indian chasing game where the active pursuer hands over by tapping a seated teammate on the back.
Play is divided into units that last up to two minutes each, and they can be ended early.
The first scorer to break clear of the group earns the right to end the unit of play whenever they choose.
The scoring player on each team wears a helmet cover with a star on it.
Blockers form a pack, and a jammer scores a point for each opponent lapped during a jam.
A full-contact race on quad skates around an oval flat track.
clues.ref: The Rules of Flat Track Roller Derby

clues.text: A whistle sounds at 60 seconds, and the routine must end at the final whistle at 90 seconds.
The apparatus for under-19 boys stands 2.6–2.8 m above the ground.
Each apparatus at an official championship is judged by four judges and a chief judge.
In school competitions, boys perform on a wooden pole and girls on a hanging rope.
Traditional Indian gymnastics performed on a vertical wooden pole or rope.
The exposed partner may not call attention to an irregularity during play.
A call that doesn't outrank the previous one is 'insufficient', and there are detailed laws for correcting it.
Failing to follow suit when you could have is a serious infringement with its own penalties.
After the bidding, declarer plays both their own hand and dummy's hand, which is laid face up.
Four-player partnership card game: bid a contract, then try to win that many tricks.
Most competitions allow a maximum of five substitutes per team.
When three or more defenders form a wall at a free kick, attackers must stay at least 1 m away from it.
All verbal offences are penalised with an indirect free kick.
A penalty kick is taken from a mark 11 m (12 yds) in front of the goal.
There's a 2-minute interval between the first and second quarters.
A team must bring the ball into its attacking half within 8 seconds.
After an offensive rebound off the rim, the shot clock resets to 14 seconds.
A basket from inside the arc scores 2 points, and each free throw scores 1.
Players get 90 seconds when changing ends, and 120 seconds at the end of each set.
No more than 25 seconds may pass between the end of one point and the start of the next.
Players change ends after the first, third and every following odd game of each set.
The court is 23.77 m long, and the net is 0.914 m high at the centre.
In stroke play, signing a scorecard showing fewer strokes than you actually took means disqualification.
A ball embedded in its own pitch-mark in the general area may be lifted and dropped without penalty.
When taking relief, you must drop the ball straight down from knee height.
On the putting green, you may leave the flagstick in the hole or have it removed before you putt.
The [object] must weigh between 156 g and 170 g, and every one used in competition must be approved.
Having too many players on the playing surface at once is a two-minute bench penalty.
Attacking players may not enter the attacking zone ahead of the [object]. If they do, play stops for offside.
A goal counts only when the puck completely crosses the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar.
The bat may be no thicker than 2.61 inches and no longer than 42 inches.
The four corners of the diamond are 90 feet apart.
With runners on base, an illegal motion by the pitcher is a balk, and every runner advances one base.
A fair ball hit over the outfield fence on the fly is a home run.
The central strip of play is 22 yards (20.12 m) long and 10 ft wide.
A hit that clears the boundary without bouncing scores six runs.
A batter is run out if the fielders break the wicket while the batter is out of their ground.
The bowler delivers overarm at the stumps, and the batter defends them with a flat bat.
Sixteen [objects] are delivered per period, with the teams taking turns.
A line 4 inches wide sits 21 ft (6.401 m) in front of the centre of each target.
Behind the tee line, only one player from each team may sweep at a time.
The skip stands in the house directing teammates who slide granite stones down a sheet of ice.
The ball must weigh 260–280 g and measure 65–67 cm around.
A back-row player who reaches above the top of the net to stop an attack commits a fault.
The libero may not block or attempt a block, individually or with teammates.
Six players a side hit a ball over a high net, scoring on every rally.
A match is played as the best of any odd number of games.
In doubles, the serve must go diagonally from the server's right half to the receiver's right half.
A serve that touches the net assembly and then lands correctly is a let and is replayed.
Players use rubber-covered rackets to hit a small ball back and forth over a net on a table.
A team that fails to appear on the field at least 10 minutes before the scheduled start loses its coin-toss option.
The offense has 40 seconds on the play clock between plays to start the next one.
A hip-drop tackle is a foul: 15 yards and an automatic first down.
Kicking the ball between the uprights from scrimmage is a field goal worth 3 points.
Every foul is worth at least four points to the opponent.
If the white comes to rest touching a ball you can play, you must play away from it without moving it.
Colours are re-spotted after being potted until all the reds are gone. Pink is worth 6 and blue 5.
A penalty or free kick may be taken from where it was awarded or anywhere behind it on a straight line.
A player must not attempt to kick the ball out of the ball-carrier's hands.
Teams must form the lineout within 15 seconds of the touch judge's signal.
If foul play stops a probable try, the referee awards a penalty try between the posts.
The penalty spots are 150 mm in diameter.
When play restarts with a bully, all other players must be at least 5 metres away.
Field players must not stop, kick, pick up, throw or carry the ball with any part of their body.
Played with hooked sticks on turf. The player taking a penalty stroke must not feint at the ball.
The net must be 760 mm deep and at least 6.1 metres wide.
Players get a break of up to 60 seconds when the leading score reaches 11, and 120 seconds between games.
When serving, it's a fault to miss the [object] entirely.
The strung area of the racket may be no more than 280 mm long and 220 mm wide.
Players use light rackets to hit a feathered shuttlecock over a high net, and it must not touch the floor.
Players are not permitted to wear jeans.
Anything that bounces off or falls out of the target can't be thrown again.
Your opponent must stand at least 60 cm behind you while you throw.
A raised oche, 38 mm high and 610 mm long, marks the minimum throwing distance.
A turn is at most three throws at a numbered board ringed with doubles and trebles.
It's forbidden to write down your moves in advance, unless you're claiming a draw.
If you claim a draw incorrectly, your opponent gets two extra minutes.
In a blitz game, all moves must be completed in 10 minutes or less per player.
Bishops, rooks and queens may not jump over other pieces.
The trophies for second and third place must be between 35 cm and 45 cm tall.
Teams may do no more than ten days of testing per year.
During a neutralised period, competitors must stay within ten car lengths of the one in front.
The pit exit opens 40 minutes before the formation lap and stays open for ten minutes.
Single-seater Grand Prix racing, where teams choose between soft, medium and hard tyres.
Undressing on the strip is forbidden.
A knockout bout ends when someone reaches 15 hits or after nine minutes of actual fighting time.
It's forbidden to hit with the guard. Any hit made that way is annulled.
A red card gives the opponent a penalty hit, and a black card means exclusion from the competition.
Bouts on a piste with foil, épée or sabre, where an electric scoring box registers each touch.
A player who is ordered off sits out four minutes of playing time.
A ball thrown in from the sideline must be touched by someone before it goes out again.
The player taking a throw-in may not step onto the court until they've released the ball.
At the centre pass, the Centre must have at least one foot wholly inside the centre circle.
Seven a side with fixed positions like Wing Attack and Goal Keeper, and infringements give penalty passes.
For a record to count, the water must contain less than 3 grams of salt per litre.
At the Olympic Games, the water must be at least 2.5 metres deep.
Each racing channel must be at least 2.5 metres wide.
At a backstroke start, standing in the gutter or curling your toes over its lip is prohibited.
Racing in pool lanes, where athletes must not obstruct or interfere with each other.
An appeal to the Jury of Appeal must be made within 30 minutes.
At 'On your marks', both hands and at least one knee must touch the ground.
For races from 200 m to 1000 m, at least 90 minutes must pass between rounds.
In the high jump and pole vault, three consecutive failures eliminate an athlete.
Sprinters start from blocks and must stay in their own lane.
A player may not grab an opponent's [implement] with an open hand or fingers.
After an injury to a defender, the shot clock resets to 80 seconds.
Attackers may not move into and make contact with a defender while setting a screen.
A face-off may never be held closer than 18 metres (20 yards) to the goal.
Ten players with netted sticks, and a goalkeeper defending a circular crease.
Individual athletes get 30 seconds per shot, or 20 seconds when shooting alternately.
Lighted tracer nocks are not allowed.
Athletes may not raise their bow arm until the signal to start shooting.
Arrows are shot at a ringed target, and a yellow light warns 30 seconds before time runs out.
Half-time can last up to 20 minutes.
The break between the first and second quarters is at most 6 minutes.
A team found with too many players on the ground concedes a fifty-metre penalty.
The outer behind posts must be at least three metres tall.
Kicks, handballs and marks on a large oval, where a free kick can be advanced 50 metres for further infringement.
Studs on boots must not have sharp edges.
When a penalty is awarded, the offending team must retire 10 metres.
A goal kicked from a penalty is worth two points.
After kicking a penalty into touch, the team restarts with a tap kick 10 metres in from touch.
Thirteen-a-side code where each team gets six tackles per set of possession.
A team must have at least five players on court at the start of the game.
If extra time is needed, it's two halves of 5 minutes after a 5-minute break.
During a throw-in, opponents must stay at least 3 metres from the thrower.
A suspension always lasts 2 minutes, and a player's third suspension means disqualification.
After a 7-metre throw, the thrower and teammates can't play the ball again until it touches an opponent or the goal.
Players may not place any object within the court.
The warm-up lasts up to 4 minutes, and players change sides after 2.
A player whose pre-existing wound starts bleeding, such as a nosebleed, gets up to 5 minutes to stop it.
A player injured by the opponent gets up to 15 minutes to recover, but only 3 if they caused the injury themselves.
Players may not leave the four-walled court during a game without the referee's permission.
Spectators must never be consulted on any line call.
The server must serve within 10 seconds of the score being called, or it's a fault.
A player must not catch or carry the ball on their [hitting implement].
A player found using a non-compliant paddle must switch to a legal one, with no penalty.
Paddle sport with a perforated plastic ball, where a technical foul for extreme unsportsmanlike conduct costs one point.
Every delivery must be made entirely by hand, so no mechanical device may propel the [object].
[Targets] knocked down by another one bouncing off the side partition or rear cushion still count.
When the head target is knocked down but separated ones remain standing after the first delivery, it's called a split.
Three strikes in a row is called a triple or a turkey.
Twelve strikes in a row produces the maximum score of 300.
Correct dress is required, and playing without a top is specifically forbidden.
A team that hasn't arrived within 30 minutes of the start is eliminated.
If the small target gets knocked away and can't be found, the search is limited to 5 minutes.
While the umpire is measuring, players must stand at least 2 metres away.
Each boule must be between 7.05 cm and 8 cm in diameter.
Players may not change the number on their headwear during a match without a referee's permission.
A team's start list must include at least seven players.
When a free throw is awarded, opponents must be at least 1 metre from the ball.
In league tables, a team that loses after a penalty shootout still earns 1 point.
A personal foul is recorded for every exclusion foul or penalty foul in the pool.
Sweep blades must be at least 5 mm thick.
Two minutes before the start time, the starter announces 'Two minutes'.
Lightweight competitors are weighed between one and two hours before their first race.
A single sculler who has entered can't be replaced except in specific circumstances.
Crews of one, two, four or eight race oared boats along a buoyed regatta course.
A competitor who turns up in the wrong colour uniform gets a maximum of one minute to change.
A competitor can't be called for a new bout until 20 minutes of rest have passed since their last one.
Coaches must stay at the foot of the platform, or at least two metres from the edge of the competition area.
After each caution, the opponent automatically receives at least one point.
After a passivity call, a 30-second mandatory-score period begins on the mat.
Before calling an obstruction, a defender may wait up to two seconds to see whether it affects play.
Each team must have no more than seven and no fewer than five players on the field.
After a turnover, play must restart within 10 seconds in mid-field, or within 20 seconds in a scoring area.
A time-out lasts 75 seconds, and afterwards the stall count restarts at nine.
Self-officiated, non-contact games that last around 100 minutes, where you can't run with the disc.
A coach may swap any team members between rounds, as long as the team stays within its weight-class maximum.
A team that loses a member may carry on with seven, but no fewer.
Teams that fail to actively compete for a set time have their inactivity flagged by the chief judge.
A pulling member who is replaced may not compete in any later match of that weight class.
Eight pullers per team, in weight classes, heave on a rope with an anchor at the back.
In unofficial national 'A' team matches, up to ten substitutes may be used.
A penalty shoot-out is not considered part of the match.
The referees may not play advantage after a breach of the four-second limit.
A goalkeeper who controls the ball in their own half for more than four seconds concedes an indirect free kick.
Five-a-side indoor football, officiated by a referee and a second referee on opposite sidelines.
Repeated serious infractions can bring a suspension of 192 weeks.
Half-time may not exceed ten minutes.
A shoulder-to-shoulder charge is allowed, but only if the player has at least one foot on the ground.
When the ball goes over the sideline, opponents must be at least 13 m away until it's kicked or thrown in.
Penalty kicks are taken off the ground, 11 m from the goal line, and points go over the bar.
The goalposts must be at least 7 metres tall.
Players may not cross the 20 m line or arc until a defensive free has been struck.
After an exceptional stoppage, play restarts on the 20 m line, and no score may be made directly from that restart.
When a team plays the ball over the sideline, the opponents restart with a free puck from the ground.
The player taking a free must lift the sliotar with the hurley at the first attempt and strike it.
When restarting after a period, the umpires must not wait for players who delay.
If a player falls, the umpire doesn't stop play unless they believe the player is hurt.
A ball that passes directly over either goal post doesn't score.
Penalty 2 is a free hit from 30 yards, Penalty 3 from 40 yards, and Penalty 4 from 60 yards.
Mounted players line up as the umpire bowls the ball hard between them from at least five yards.
Plastic or hard visors are not allowed as part of the uniform.
The safety grip on a bat may be no more than two layers thick.
The hitter must take position within 10 seconds of the umpire declaring 'Play ball.'
A pitcher who returns to pitch in the same half inning doesn't get more warm-up pitches.
An 11-inch (27.9 cm) ball is pitched underhand, in an arc, to the batter.
Each set lasts up to three minutes on the set clock.
At the start signal, every player must have at least one foot on the back line.
A player must not use any part of their uniform or clothing to help make a catch.
Out players wait in a queue to return when a teammate catches a throw. Benches sit at least 4 m from the centre line.
The [hitting implement] may not contain any device that could communicate with or advise the player.
A 3-minute courtesy warm-up rally between the players is obligatory.
When serving, you may not touch the service line or the imaginary centre line with your feet.
Each player receives serve alternately, and once the order is set it can't be changed.
Doubles in a walled court where the net can be at most 1.05 m high at the posts, and a tie-break goes to 7.
The playing area must be surrounded by a free zone at least 3 m wide on all sides.
Requested time-outs last 30 seconds.
No more than 12 seconds may pass between the end of a rally and the whistle for the next serve.
There are strict rules on overhand finger contact: the ball must not come to rest in the fingers.
On sand, a serving-team player must not screen the server from the opponents' view.
The marker for a live target in the ditch may be no more than 50 mm wide and 100 mm high.
If both players deliver the small target improperly in the same period, it isn't delivered again. It's placed centrally instead.
Markers dividing the playing areas must be no more than 430 mm high.
If a wrongly marked toucher can't have its chalk removed without disturbing the head, it's treated as a non-toucher.
Players deliver from a mat toward the jack, and a re-spotted jack doesn't make the end dead.
The striker may not use artificial aids to help judge a stroke.
A player found seeking advice during a game can be penalised.
When replacing a ball, the striker may not rotate it to change its alignment.
The peg point can't be scored while you're playing the wrong ball.
In handicap games, weaker players get 'bisques', extra turns that may not be split into halves.
The court must be a level rectangle 8–10 feet wide.
Each target is made of smooth plywood with a surface 2 feet wide.
If you accidentally drop your [object] before your swing starts, it isn't a foul and you can pick it up.
A judge can declare a foul bag, which must be removed from the board.
Players toss bean bags at a board with a hole, using cancellation scoring up to 21.
Placing any object as a directional aid is not allowed.
Taking excessive time earns a warning first, and a penalty for a repeat.
Intentionally interfering with another player's thrown [object] costs you two penalty throws.
If the two-meter rule is in effect, a disc that comes to rest two meters or more above the ground costs a penalty.
Golf played with flying discs, where moving a spectator rope and not restoring it costs a one-throw penalty.
Coaches' positions must be marked at least 2 m from the competition area.
After a decision, the judges must record the winner within 10 seconds with their heads down.
At most two coaches and one medical staff member may enter the field of play.
After a passivity penalty, the opponent's points count double for the next ten seconds.
Kicks to the head score most, and a concussion brings at least 30 days of mandatory medical suspension.
The teeth of the brake must be at least 20 mm high.
The steel the vehicle glides on must not be harder than 385 Brinell.
If the vehicle stops before the finish line, the team is disqualified, and outside help isn't allowed.
During a competition, pilots may not make extra runs on the track outside official training and the race.
Competitions include two-person and four-person sleds, plus the women's monobob.
One piece of adhesive tape, up to a maximum size, is allowed on the helmet's chin guard.
Before the second weight check, athletes get up to 5 minutes to remove snow and ice from their equipment.
No more than 12 training heats are offered per competition.
The sled's cowling must be convex, with no more than 3 mm of concavity over 300 mm.
Athletes slide head-first, and at least three forerunner sleds test the ice track before races.
A composition made of a series of unrelated elements is penalised.
The time judge deducts 0.05 for each second a routine runs over or under.
Every body difficulty must include at least one technical element with the handheld equipment.
If the apparatus breaks mid-routine, the gymnast may remove it from the floor area without penalty.
Routines to music must include a dance-steps combination lasting at least 8 seconds, with hoop, ball, clubs or ribbon.
Yellow flags mark each end of the imaginary lines that define the penalty area.
At a corner kick, opponents must stay at least 5 m from the imaginary corner arc.
A penalty kick may be taken by any player, or even a substitute, from the team awarded it.
When the ball crosses the sideline, play restarts with either a kick-in or a throw-in.
Played on sand, and a match can't end in a draw: extra time and then penalties decide it.
Player numbers must be at least 10 inches (25 cm) high.
A game is 60 minutes of actual playing time, in four periods of 15 minutes.
On a kick-off from a tee, the lowest point of the ball may be no more than 1 inch above the ground.
A player receiving a hand-off must not be lined up in a lineman's position at that moment.
Three downs to make 10 yards on a 110-yard field, with 12 players a side.
Team coaches must stay in their designated area and must not coach from elsewhere around the field.
A team has at most 14 players, and no more than six of them on the field at once.
A player in possession may not kick the ball.
At a rollball, the attacker rolls the ball back between their feet no more than one metre.
Rugby without tackles, where defenders must not deliberately knock the ball from the carrier's hands.
A field player lying on the playing surface is considered out of the game and may not play the ball.
At the start, players must stay in their own half and can't cross the centre line until the ball is played.
Players serving timed penalties may take part in a penalty shootout, but players expelled for the whole game may not.
A penalty stroke isn't complete until the ball leaves the penalty area or a goal is scored.
Eleven skaters chase a small ball with curved sticks, and offences can bring a 10-minute penalty.
The only alteration allowed to the goalkeeper's face mask is painting it.
If penalty shots after overtime leave a team without a goalkeeper, it has at most 3 minutes to equip one.
At a face-off, the players taking it must not make physical contact with each other.
Socks worn over shoes aren't allowed, and a player who loses a shoe may keep playing until the next stoppage.
Indoor stick sport in a low-walled rink, where serious offences bring a match penalty.
Goalkeepers may wear a neck protector no more than 5 cm high.
When a team wins the ball in its defensive zone, it has ten seconds to move it out.
Padded gloves may be no more than 2.5 cm thick.
Goalkeepers may not use their special protective equipment to play the ball outside the penalty area.
On roller skates, a goalkeeper outside the penalty area who plays the ball with their gloves commits a foul.
Captains' letters must be at least 7.62 cm (3 in) tall.
For a penalty shot, the shooter is chosen from the players who were on the playing surface at the time.
A minor penalty is cancelled if the opposing team scores while it's being served.
A goal is nullified if a penalty occurs before the ring enters the net.
Ice game played with a straight stick and a rubber ring, with a 30-second shot clock.
A team must have at least twelve players to start a match.
Every player must wear a helmet with a facial guard.
A team may make a maximum of 8 substitutions.
When a clashed sliotar crosses the sideline, play restarts with a throw-in.
The women's game with hurleys, where a sideline puck must be taken promptly once the sliotar is placed.
Goal judges don't change ends at half-time.
Each team may name a maximum of 5 substitutes.
The field of play may be no more than 170 yards long.
A warning for persistent fouling is issued after a minimum of three fouls.
In a penalty play-off, each team nominates five players to strike at goal with their caman.
Players may not hang on the floating ropes that mark the team substitution areas.
A player dismissed for the rest of the match must go to the designated penalty box.
The [implement] must not extend beyond the hand by more than 25 mm.
At a penalty shot, attacking players may immediately submerge and move to any legal position.
Played on the pool floor, where a defender at a penalty shot tries to push the puck back across a 6 m line.
There's no limit on the height of the animals ridden, as long as they're fit and safe.
An umpire may sideline a player for at most three minutes of playing time.
Roping saddles, or any saddle with a horn, may not be used.
The umpire won't stop play for a broken or dropped racquet unless it's dangerous.
Played on horseback, where a wild or dangerous swing of the racquet is penalised.
The bat must be a round staff no more than 70 mm thick.
Teams have no more than nine players each.
The player delivering the ball may take no more than two steps.
A fielder may not stand on a base or on the lines between bases.
Irish bat-and-ball game played with a hurling ball, where a batter may not stand in front of home base.
The pole holding the target must not stick up above the top of the basket.
In certain situations, the shot clock resets to 25 seconds.
You can't run with the ball: you must release it before your foot lands again.
A penalty is taken by the attacker who was denied a free scoring chance.
Mixed teams shoot at a basket on a tall post, and drawn matches can go to a golden goal.
Jewellery that could cause injury, like rings or brooches, is forbidden.
A match is three periods of 15 minutes.
Holding the ball for more than 3 seconds is a fault.
After a breakdown in play, at least one pass must be made before shooting at a frame.
The attacking team scores if the ball rebounds off the frame and touches a defender inside the forbidden zone.
When stepping in, the referee should stand about two metres from the ball.
A 2-minute break is allowed between periods.
At a kick-off or restart, the team has 5 seconds to hit the ball.
A hit must send the ball at least 1.8 m (6 ft) measured along the ground, or it's a short-hit fault.
Three teams share one giant ball, and a defender within 1.83 m who blocks the hitter commits illegal defence.
Referees may not touch players without first announcing their intent.
When the 15-second audible signal sounds, the referees call out '15 seconds'.
Players must not be re-orientated by people on the bench, only by the referee or goal judge.
A throw must touch the court at least once on or before the High Ball Line, 6 m out.
Three players a side, and during sudden-death extra throws, nobody may touch their eyeshades.
A one-minute penalty expires once the player has spent one minute of game time in the penalty box.
Disregarding an official's directive earns a yellow card.
Incidental contact with a dodgeball being held by another player is not penalised.
Illegally pursuing the flag sends a player back to touch their hoops.
Beaters throw dodgeballs, and there are special interference rules for the third dodgeball.
Anti-tip devices must have two wheels at least 40 cm apart, centre to centre.
The posts marking the scoring line must be at least 45 cm high.
A player touching the ball may not touch the floor with any part of their body.
If the total player ratings on court, including the penalty box, exceed the maximum, it's a technical foul.
Each possession is timed by a 'Forty Second Operator' in this four-a-side wheelchair sport.
Players may not play in socks only or in bare feet.
Injured players get a total of 15 minutes of rest across the whole match.
An equipment timeout may not exceed 30 seconds.
In the three-wall version, the front wall is at least 20 ft wide and 20 ft high.
Interference in an enclosed court is either a replay hinder or, if it blocks a shot to the front wall, a penalty hinder.
Player numbers on the back must be at least 19 cm tall.
If both sides reach 20–20, the set extends to a maximum of 25 points.
The server has fifteen seconds to be ready with a foot in the service circle.
A team left with fewer than three players can't continue the game.
An injured player gets up to five minutes in this game of kicking a ball over a net.
The coin used for the toss must be at least 25 mm in diameter.
The ball's circumference must be at least 67 cm.
It's forbidden to hold the ball between two body parts.
In doubles, you may not return the ball with the same body part you used on your previous return.
Played on a curved table, and during time-outs the players may not leave the court.
The ball must weigh between 61 and 62 grams.
Each time-out may not exceed thirty seconds.
The receiver must be in the ready position within 10 seconds.
Deliberately wetting your gloves is penalised.
Strike the ball with your hand against the front wall, and a ball taken on the second hop is dead.
Taking a communication device onto the court earns a yellow card and a penalty ball.
Warm-up ends when both sides have played all their balls, or after 2 minutes.
Balls must show no visible scuff marks or abrasions beyond normal use.
A ramp may not include any mechanical device for sighting or aiming.
Each athlete brings red or blue balls into the call room, and each side brings a white jack ball.
Blades with metal tips are not allowed.
The ends of every boat must have a radius of at least 100 mm.
Players must not apply any substance to their boat that changes how it handles or grips.
Paddle blades must have integrated padding along their edges.
Five a side in kayaks, and the most serious fouls bring a red card and ejection.
At the end of a contest, constant screaming and cheering aren't allowed.
An absent athlete is called twice, 30 seconds apart. Thirty seconds after the second call, the opponent wins.
In the visually impaired version, you may not assist your grip with your other hand.
'Hajime' and penalties are always given from the starting position.
Grip-based Olympic martial art, where illegal grips are punished with a shido.
Pointing a finger at the umpire to demand a decision is a foul.
Coaching from outside the court, by coaches or players, is a foul.
Two yellow cards mean the next card is red, and a yellow card means a 2-minute suspension.
A suspended player's two minutes only start once they're back on court after being revived.
In this raiding game, a green card is a warning, and two greens mean the next card is yellow.
The hand-off between teammates must not be given to an outstretched arm or leg.
There's a 6-minute interval after each innings, and a shorter break between turns.
An attacker may not go into the other half of the court except as the rules allow.
Each innings consists of a chasing turn and a running turn.
Indian chasing game where attackers try to tag defenders, who run in batches.
Penalties must be called loudly enough for the penalised player to hear.
A player waiting in the queue may return to the penalty box once there's space.
A player who doesn't immediately give up a teammate's helmet cover can be penalised.
Only the jammer and the pivot may control the star. Other skaters may not.
The jammer may pass the star to the pivot, who then becomes the scoring skater.
Different apparatus must be spaced at least 10 metres apart.
Competitors get 3 minutes to warm up and get ready.
All hold positions must be held for 2 seconds.
There's no minimum time limit for the compulsory set.
Routines on a wooden pole or rope, where an optional set shorter than 60 or longer than 90 seconds is penalised.
A player may not ask a question when its only purpose is to help their partner.
Calls and plays must be made without special emphasis, mannerism or inflection.
A defender's card exposed by accident may become a 'penalty card' that must be played at the first legal chance.
If a defender leads out of turn, declarer may accept the lead or require it to be withdrawn.
Partnership card game where declarer plays both hands, and the same deals are replayed at other tables.
